notes: Period 6 occurs: a 6-cycle at p = 1009 (Lean cycle1009, period_six_1009), so the known lengths are 2, 4, 6. Exhaustive census p <= 31: only the standard 4-cycle. Random search (200 starts per prime, 1000 < p < 4000): 32 two-cycles, 2 four-cycles, the 6-cycle. Small-support search (all cycles reachable from sets of size <= 2 for p <= 593, <= 3 for p <= 139, <= 4 for p <= 59): periods 2 and 4 only; 2-cycles at p = 71, 127, 151 (2), 181, 367, 373, 397, 409, 421 (2), 431, 449; a non-standard 4-cycle at p = 541. Lean: cycle71, cycle127, cycle151, cycle541 (decide +kernel, no axioms), zero_alternates (evenness of every period; propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Outside Lean: the census and searches (C programs phi_exh.c, phi_small.c, phi_rand.c).

sources.cite: R. Froberg, S. Lundqvist, A. Oneto, B. Shapiro, Algebraic stories from one and from the other pockets, Arnold Math. J. 4 (2018), 4.3

prior_art.note: Census p <= 31, period 6 and the new cycles are not in the literature found.
